question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\operatorname{tan}⁡{15}^{∘}=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12})$

II. $\operatorname{tan}⁡{20}^{∘}=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{36})$

III. $\operatorname{tan}⁡{35}^{∘}=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{36})$
question.worked_solution:
Let's examine the statements one by one.

- Statement I is true. Converting ${15}^{∘}$ from degrees to radians, we get

$$
{15}^{∘}=15\cdot \frac{\pi }{180}=\frac{\pi }{12}\,\text{radians}.
$$

- Statement II is false. Converting ${20}^{∘}$ from degrees to radians, we get

$$
{20}^{∘}=20\cdot \frac{\pi }{180}=\frac{\pi }{9}\,\text{radians}.
$$

The statement is false because $\frac{\pi }{9}\ne \frac{5\pi }{36}.$

- Statement III is true. Converting ${35}^{∘}$ from degrees to radians, we get 

$$
{35}^{∘}=35\cdot \frac{\pi }{180}=\frac{7\pi }{36}\,\text{radians}.
$$

So, the correct answer is 'I and III only'.
